articles.author: Mateo Perez Salazar
articles.description:
I’m building Archseed, and I’ve reached an uncomfortable point: some developers like the idea, a few have tried it, but nobody has bought the Pro plan.
Rather than post another feature announcement, I’d like to understand what I might be getting wrong.
The problem I’m trying to solve
What belongs in V1?
What should explicitly stay out?
Which architectural patterns should it follow?
Which assumptions need your approval before implementation?
My hypothesis is that making those decisions explicit before coding can help avoid unwanted scope and architectural choices.
For example, “build a booking app” leaves a lot unanswered. Does V1 need payments? Multiple businesses? Customer accounts? An agent can produce a plausible implementation without those decisions matching what you intended.
What Archseed does
It’s not another coding agent, and it isn’t meant to replace your IDE.
An important limitation: generating Markdown does not automatically enforce architecture or guarantee that an agent will follow every decision. I don’t want to pretend otherwise.
Where I’m stuck
Some people have responded positively, but that hasn’t translated into paid users. Recent outreach also hasn’t led to many new trials.
I don’t yet know whether:
The problem isn’t painful enough.
The benefit isn’t clear enough to justify trying another tool.
Developers already solve it well enough with their agent’s planning workflow and project instructions.
A subscription is the wrong fit for something they mainly need when starting a project.
I don’t want to assume that lowering the price would fix the underlying issue.
What I’d like to learn
And looking at Archseed’s approach, what—if anything—would it add to your current workflow?
“I already handle this with my coding agent” is useful feedback too, especially if you can explain how.
You don’t need to install anything to reply. I’m more interested in understanding your experience than collecting signups.
Project: Archseed
articles.title: I built a planning CLI for AI coding agents. Some developers like the idea, but nobody has bought Pro. What am I missing?

Introduction
React is known for its efficient rendering process, and one of the key techniques it utilizes is batching. articles.author: Saurabh Pathak
articles.description:
My last post was about human approval for destructive MCP tools. The comments taught me more than the code did, so I want to put the points together and ask what you think is still missing.
What readers pointed out
Bind approval to the exact action. Hash the arguments at preview and check the same hash at execute, so a retry or a changed id can't run something the human never saw (@paul_irolla_6b5ae261d0224, @jes_p_d4f61f7aa2ec405a418).
Resolve context, not just the tool name. click(element_id) can be harmless or a payment. Gate on the resolved label, and re-resolve right before execute in case the UI changed (@autenai).
Make most things cheap to be wrong about. Classify tools by reversibility. A delete can move files to a quarantine folder with a TTL, and the human gate is kept for truly irreversible actions (@shuttlewright).
Approvals expire. Require a matching, unexpired approval id at execute time, and keep an append-only journal the agent can't write to (@eye_java_420f1faa10ae8b86).
Refuse by default. If a client can't do elicitation, irreversible tools should be refused, and token mode should be a named, per-tool opt-in (@kami_butt_69b922ade8de012).
A script can answer elicitation. In Claude Code a hook can return "accept" with no dialog, so the server can't tell a click from a script (@skillselion).
Where the project stands
The project is a small first version. None of the ideas above are built yet except the strict true-only autoApprove rule and per-path allowlists. I'm planning to add them step by step, and I'd rather say that plainly than overclaim.
Questions for you
Which of these would you build first?
What is the worst "approved by mistake" incident you've seen with an agent?
Is there a gate I haven't listed?
It's open source, so issues and PRs are very welcome.
articles.title: What should an approval gate for AI agents actually bind to? Lessons from the comments
